_comment: Single source of truth for every pinned upstream version/URL CoDebian bundles or downloads. Bump values here only -- app/build.gradle.kts's :app:generateRemoteAssets task turns this into dev.codebian.app.RemoteAssets at build time, and scripts/fetch-assets.ps1 / scripts/fetch-assets.sh both read it directly, so there is exactly one place to update per release.

debianRootfs._comment: Pulled from Docker Hub's registry (see DockerRegistryClient.kt / fetch-assets scripts) rather than a static tarball URL, so republishing the same tag keeps working without re-pinning a URL by hand.

codeServer._comment: Exact GitHub release + its arm64 .deb asset digest, bundled into the APK at build time (see ensureCodeServerInstalled in BootstrapService.kt) so first-run install no longer depends on 'latest' upstream install.sh staying reachable. The in-app 'Update code-server' button still installs genuinely-latest online, on demand.

aptSnapshot._comment: Pins the rootfs's /etc/apt sources to a fixed snapshot.debian.org timestamp (see pinAptToSnapshot in BootstrapService.kt) so git/python3/nodejs (and anything else apt-installed) keep resolving to the exact same packages forever, immune to the live 'trixie' suite moving on or a package being superseded -- snapshot.debian.org keeps every version indefinitely. Bump this occasionally (e.g. yearly) to pick up security fixes; it is not required to track 'today'.

nodejs._comment: NodeSource's setup_lts.x always resolves to whatever is current LTS *at curl time*, a moving target that can silently change behavior on a rebuild months later. Pinning an explicit major version series (NodeSource keeps setup_<N>.x working long after a newer LTS ships) removes that surprise; bump deliberately when a new LTS is desired.
